did_you_know.text: Did you know? The inner gate facing east remains closed during the six weekdays, but it is opened on the Sabbath and on the New Moon.
Did you know? On Sabbaths and New Moons, the common people bow down before the Lord at the opened eastern gate.
Did you know? On the Sabbath, the prince offers six unblemished lambs and one unblemished ram; the amount of grain offering for the lambs is not fixed but is given according to his ability.

Did you know? During the appointed festivals, the people enter through one gate and leave through the opposite gate: those who enter through the north leave through the south, and those who enter through the south leave through the north. The prince also enters and leaves among the people.
Did you know? When the prince brings a freewill burnt offering or fellowship offering on a weekday, the eastern gate is opened for him; after he leaves, it is closed.
Did you know? Every morning, a year-old unblemished lamb is offered as the regular burnt offering.
Did you know? The regular burnt offering also includes a grain offering of fine flour and oil in fixed quantities, and it is established as a lasting ordinance and a regular burnt offering.

Did you know? A gift that the prince gives to one of his servants remains with that servant until the year of release; afterward, it returns to the prince. But a son’s inheritance passes to his descendants.
Did you know? Ezekiel emphasizes that the prince may not take any of the people’s inheritance to enrich his sons; instead, he must give them an inheritance from his own property.
Did you know? At the four corners of the outer court are cooking courts of equal size: forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide.
